updateCadence: Tracks Chromium closely via the secureblue repo
summary: Trivalent is a security-focused Chromium build for desktop Linux from the secureblue project. It adds hardening patches, makes extras like the password manager and search suggestions opt-in, and is built for Fedora Atomic systems.
bestFor: secureblue and Fedora users who want a hardened browser
Security-minded Linux users who accept Chromium
People who liked Vanadium on Android
notFor: People who need Manifest V2 extensions
Anyone who wants a polished installer on any distro

pros.title: Hardening patches
pros.detail: Adds patches and sandbox flags on top of Fedora’s Chromium, ported partly from Vanadium.

pros.title: Opt-in extras
pros.detail: The password manager and search suggestions are opt-in by default.

pros.title: Strict defaults
pros.detail: Strict pop-up blocking and Chromium’s subresource filter are enabled.

cons.title: Fedora-centric
cons.detail: Official support is only through secureblue; other installs are unsupported.

cons.title: No MV2
cons.detail: The project treats re-enabling Manifest V2 as out of scope for security reasons.

cons.title: No clear release page
cons.detail: The GitHub Releases section is empty; versions come from the repo.

faq.q: How is Trivalent related to Vanadium?
faq.a: It is inspired by Vanadium and includes Vanadium’s desktop-relevant patches.

faq.q: Can I install it on any Linux distribution?
faq.a: Official support is only through secureblue; Fedora users can install from the secureblue repo unofficially.
Yes. The repo includes GPL-2.0 licensing alongside Chromium’s own licenses.

timeline.event: Project starts as secureblue’s hardened browser (not verified)

switching.note: Standard Chromium profile and import paths; sync availability is not documented.
